lineage.strategy: Use fresh primary operating evidence to frame demand concentration and scale-economics risk, explicitly preserving the coexistence of rapid growth and reduced guidance.

observedWeaknesses.observation: Q2 revenue grew rapidly year over year, yet Serve reduced full-year revenue guidance to $9M-$10M because Uber Eats delivery volume was below expectations; revenue remains small relative to the guided operating-expense base.
observedWeaknesses.whyItMatters: Headline growth does not eliminate partner-demand, utilization or scale-economics risk; weaker volume through a major partner directly changed the annual outlook.

risks.risk: Dependence on partner delivery volume can produce utilization and revenue volatility, while the current revenue base remains small relative to operating expense and sustainable per-robot economics are not yet demonstrated.

falsifiers.condition: Subsequent source-addressed results show diversified demand, sustained utilization, improving gross economics and revenue scaling materially faster than operating expense without renewed guidance reductions.
falsifiers.effect: Would reduce concentration and scale-economics concerns.

improvementPaths: Demonstrate diversified partner demand, per-robot economics, utilization and gross-margin progression as fleet scale increases.

unknowns.unknown: Sustainable per-robot economics, gross-margin breakeven timing and partner-level concentration remain unproven at current scale.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid year-over-year revenue growth coexists with reduced annual revenue guidance caused by weaker Uber Eats delivery volume; growth rate alone is not sufficient evidence of execution quality.

recommendation: Use the demand-concentration and scale-economics evidence in Alpha risk construction without assigning a numeric risk score.
